adds.title: Guyana Government CEDAW Ninth Periodic Report - Geneva presentation July 2019 by Minister of Social Protection Amna Ally
adds.summary: Article 149 of Guyana's revised Constitution guarantees equality and non-discrimination, and in July 2019 the Government recognized responsibility to remove legal gaps to prevent discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity with active stakeholder dialogue toward filling them, affirmed every individual regardless of sexual orientation/gender identity has the right to live free from violence, abuse and discrimination while condemning a recent attack on a leading LGBTQ activist, and reported Society Against Sexual Orientation Discrimination cooperation with the Guyana Police Force hierarchy to retrain/train officers to respond professionally to LGBTQ complaints and service access alongside cabinet approval of a sexual and reproductive health policy inclusive of sexual orientation.

adds.title: Society Against Sexual Orientation Discrimination (SASOD) - Law Reform Commission advocacy and police extortion / hate-crime reporting; Ministry of Social Protection condemnation
adds.summary: On 13 November 2018 the Caribbean Court of Justice struck out the cross-dressing prohibition in the Summary Jurisdiction Act as unenforceable though the text remains, while loitering and vagrancy provisions in the same Act remain enforceable and Criminal Law (Offences) Act ss.351-353 continue to criminalize male same-sex gross indecency punishable by 2 years imprisonment, attempted buggery and male indecent assault punishable by 10 years, and buggery punishable by life imprisonment. In that legal context police approach same-sex couples and LGBT persons socializing in public places including seawalls, parks, gardens late at night and cars and threaten arrest to extort bribes to avoid being taken to the station, where further discrimination impedes justice and causes hate-crime victims to file watered-down reports for fear of embarrassment. LGBT persons face persistent harassment and discrimination when using public minibuses and boats from operators and passengers, and repeal of the colonial buggery, gross indecency, loitering and vagrancy provisions was pending before the Legal Affairs Ministry's Law Reform Commission.

adds.title: Constitution of Honduras - Articles 112 and 116 (2005 amendment)
adds.summary: On 4 May 2005 Honduras by Decree 36 amended Constitution Articles 112 and 116 to provide that only a man and a woman who have that status naturally may contract marriage, prohibiting marriage and de facto union between persons of the same sex.
